name: ParikshaNet
tagline: Online entrance exams where three lakh candidates log in at 09:30 sharp
summary: ParikshaNet runs computer-based entrance and university exams for up to three lakh candidates a session: OTP login, the question paper, answer autosave, webcam proctoring, final submission and results. Every session starts with every candidate logging in within ten minutes and ends with everyone submitting at once. Login storms, lost answers and a proctoring service that slows down as the exam goes on keep coming back.

incidents.title: Candidates could not log in for 9 minutes at 09:30
incidents.desc: Two lakh candidates logged in within five minutes; login returned errors until 09:39.
whys: Login failed at 09:30
Every centre opened login at the same second
All centres start the session at 09:30 with no staggered login window
incidents.lesson: A fixed start second turns every exam into a login storm.

incidents.title: Answers lost when autosave timed out
incidents.desc: Around 900 candidates found answers missing after a page refresh at 10:45.
whys: Saved answers were missing
Autosave calls timed out against the database
Autosave writes every keystroke straight to the database
incidents.fix: Restored answers from the browser cache where possible.
incidents.lesson: Every keystroke as a database write cannot scale.

incidents.title: Proctoring snapshots stopped after two hours
incidents.desc: From 11:30 the proctoring service stopped accepting webcam snapshots and flagged candidates as absent.
whys: Snapshots were rejected after 11:30
The proctoring process ran out of memory
Frame buffers are never released after a snapshot is uploaded
incidents.lesson: A leak shows up in hour three, not in the first test.

incidents.title: OTPs arrived 6 minutes late at a 09:30 session
incidents.desc: Login OTPs were delayed by the SMS provider; candidates waited at their desks.
whys: OTPs arrived late
The SMS provider throttled the burst
OTPs go through a single SMS provider with no fallback
incidents.fix: Asked the provider to raise the limit.
incidents.lesson: One provider is one point of failure on exam morning.

incidents.title: Final submission hung at 12:30
incidents.desc: When the session ended, submissions took up to 4 minutes and some candidates saw errors.
whys: Submissions hung at the end of the session
Every submission built its answer-sheet PDF inside the request
Answer sheets are generated synchronously during submission
incidents.lesson: Everyone submits in the same minute.

incidents.title: Results page down for 40 minutes after publication
incidents.desc: Results went live at 18:00; the page timed out for most candidates.
whys: The results page timed out
Every request computed the rank card from the database
Result pages are computed on every request
incidents.lesson: Results are read a million times and written once.

incidents.title: Question images failed to load in one section
incidents.desc: Diagrams in the physics section did not load for 20 minutes.
whys: Images did not load
Media requests overloaded the paper service
The paper is decrypted and rendered on every request

incidents.title: Database failover froze autosave for 4 minutes
incidents.desc: A planned failover at 11:00 stalled every autosave and console refresh.
whys: Autosave froze during the failover
Services held connections to the old primary
Services do not retry on a database failover
incidents.fix: Restarted the services after the failover.
incidents.lesson: A failover nobody rehearsed is an outage.

incidents.title: Login storm again at the 14:30 session
incidents.desc: The afternoon session repeated the morning's login failures for 7 minutes.
whys: Login failed at 14:30
Every centre opened login at the same second again
All centres start the session at 09:30 with no staggered login window

incidents.title: Autosave errors at the half-way mark
incidents.desc: Autosave timed out for 15 minutes at 11:00 for about 2,000 candidates.
whys: Autosave failed again
Writes per second doubled at the half-way mark
Autosave writes every keystroke straight to the database

incidents.title: Proctoring flagged a whole hall as absent
incidents.desc: In the third hour, snapshots failed and 300 candidates were wrongly flagged.
whys: Snapshots failed in hour three
Proctoring memory grew until the pods were killed
Frame buffers are never released after a snapshot is uploaded

incidents.title: OTP delays during a university exam
incidents.desc: Login OTPs took up to 8 minutes; invigilators logged candidates in by hand.
whys: OTPs arrived late again
The SMS provider throttled the burst again
OTPs go through a single SMS provider with no fallback
incidents.fix: Logged candidates in from the console.

incidents.title: Submission errors at 17:30
incidents.desc: The afternoon session's submissions failed for 3 minutes.
whys: Submissions failed at the end
Answer-sheet PDFs were built inside the request
Answer sheets are generated synchronously during submission

incidents.title: Result scraping slowed the results page
incidents.desc: Coaching-centre scripts fetched thousands of rank cards a minute after results.
whys: The results page slowed down
Scripts fetched rank cards by roll number in bulk
The results page has no rate limit or CAPTCHA
incidents.lesson: Scrapers come back with new addresses.

incidents.title: Question paper load took 40 seconds
incidents.desc: At 09:30 the paper took up to 40 seconds to open.
whys: The paper took 40 seconds to load
Every candidate's request decrypted and rendered the paper
The paper is decrypted and rendered on every request
incidents.fix: Pre-rendered the paper for that exam by hand.

incidents.title: Autosave failed during a database failover
incidents.desc: An unplanned failover at 10:10 stalled autosave for 6 minutes.
whys: Autosave stalled on failover
Services kept talking to the old primary
Services do not retry on a database failover

incidents.title: Login failures at a 09:30 session
incidents.desc: The morning session saw login errors for 6 minutes.
whys: Login failed at 09:30
All centres opened together
All centres start the session at 09:30 with no staggered login window

incidents.title: Answers missing after a refresh
incidents.desc: Some candidates lost the last 5 minutes of answers when autosave timed out.
whys: Answers were missing
Autosave timed out
Autosave writes every keystroke straight to the database

incidents.title: Proctoring slowed down in hour three
incidents.desc: Snapshot uploads slowed after two and a half hours.
whys: Snapshots slowed in hour three
Proctoring memory kept growing
Frame buffers are never released after a snapshot is uploaded

incidents.title: Submissions slow at the end of the session
incidents.desc: Final submissions took two minutes at 12:30.
whys: Submissions were slow

debts.title: Queue candidate logins in staggered waves by centre
debts.desc: Admit candidates through a login queue in five waves from 09:00, by centre, and scale login up before the first wave.
debts.cause: All centres start the session at 09:30 with no staggered login window

debts.title: Failover to a second SMS provider, with email as the fallback for OTPs
debts.desc: Send OTPs through two SMS providers behind a circuit breaker that switches automatically, and by email when both are slow.
debts.cause: OTPs go through a single SMS provider with no fallback

debts.title: Pre-render the question paper and serve it cached, encrypted per session
debts.desc: Render each paper once when it is frozen, encrypt it per session key and serve it from the edge cache.
debts.cause: The paper is decrypted and rendered on every request

debts.title: Keep answers in the browser and sync with backoff
debts.desc: Store every answer locally first and sync to the server with exponential backoff, so a stall never loses answers.
debts.cause: Autosave writes every keystroke straight to the database

debts.title: Batch writes from autosave every 30 seconds
debts.desc: Write each candidate's answers in one transaction every 30 seconds instead of one write per keystroke.
debts.cause: Autosave writes every keystroke straight to the database

debts.title: Release frame buffers after each snapshot upload
debts.desc: Free the webcam frame buffer once its snapshot is stored, and add a memory alarm per pod.
debts.cause: Frame buffers are never released after a snapshot is uploaded

debts.title: Upload snapshots asynchronously through a queue to object storage
debts.desc: Let the browser upload snapshots to object storage through an upload queue with signed URLs, so the proctoring service only records flags.

debts.title: Queue final submissions and build answer sheets asynchronously
debts.desc: Accept the submission at once, queue it, and build the answer-sheet PDF in the background.
debts.cause: Answer sheets are generated synchronously during submission

debts.title: Rate limits and CAPTCHA on the results page
debts.desc: Limit rank-card lookups per device and IP and add a CAPTCHA after five lookups.
debts.cause: The results page has no rate limit or CAPTCHA

debts.title: Precompute result pages and serve them cached
debts.desc: Generate every rank card when results are frozen and serve the pages from the cache.
debts.cause: Result pages are computed on every request

debts.title: Separate connection pools for exam traffic and admin reports
debts.desc: Give candidate-facing services their own pool so console reports cannot starve autosave.

debts.title: Regression tests and canary releases for the question-paper service
debts.desc: Run regression tests on every paper release and release to one test centre first, rolling back automatically on errors.

debts.title: Paginate the live candidate grid in the invigilator console
debts.desc: Load 50 candidates per page and refresh only the ones that changed.

debts.title: Rehearse database failover and retry connections in every service
debts.desc: Run a failover drill every month and make every service reconnect with backoff.
debts.cause: Services do not retry on a database failover

debts.title: Use IST for session start times
debts.desc: Store and compare session start times in IST.

events.name: Result-scraping bots
events.description: Results go live at 18:00. Coaching centres' scripts fetch rank cards by roll number in bulk, on top of three lakh candidates checking their own.

events.name: Proctoring memory leak
events.description: A three-hour university exam. The proctoring service never frees its frame buffers, so it gets a little slower every hour until snapshots start to fail.

effects.label: Proctoring memory grows with every snapshot
effects.recovered: The exam ends and the pods are restarted

events.name: OTP delays at login
events.description: A 09:30 session. At 09:20 the SMS provider throttles ParikshaNet, and login OTPs stop arriving for an hour.

effects.label: The SMS provider throttles login OTPs

events.name: Database failover mid-exam
events.description: At 11:00, half-way through the paper, the primary database fails over. For the next hour, services that do not retry keep failing against the old primary.

effects.label: The primary database fails over; connections to it break

events.name: Question-paper release breaks images
events.description: A paper-service release goes out before the 09:30 session and breaks image rendering. The paper opens without its diagrams until the release is rolled back.

effects.label: The new paper release fails on questions with images
effects.prevented: The canary centre showed the errors, and the release was rolled back before the other centres opened the paper
